name: Stop other computers printing through this PC
summary: Make the print spooler refuse connections from other computers.
what: Sets the policy Allow Print Spooler to accept client connections to disabled. Printing from this PC is not affected.
benefit: Other computers on your network can no longer reach the print spooler here. Microsoft offered exactly this as a mitigation for the 2021 PrintNightmare flaw.
risk: Low. Other computers can no longer print through this PC, and you cannot share a printer from it. The print spooler must restart, so a restart finishes the change.
advice: Suggested if you do not share a printer from this PC. Skip it if other computers print through it.
facts: Printing from this PC to its own printers keeps working
Microsoft lists it as a mitigation for CVE-2021-34527, PrintNightmare
Enforced by a machine policy, so it applies to every account
Honored on Pro, Enterprise and Education
A restart finishes the change, because the spooler must restart

name: Skip the lock screen
summary: Go straight to sign-in after locking, with no lock screen to dismiss first.
what: Sets the policy Do not display the lock screen. After you lock the PC you see your sign-in tile directly.
benefit: One fewer click or key press every time you wake or unlock the PC.
risk: None. You sign in the same way as before. Only the lock screen step is skipped.
advice: Your choice. Turn it on if you never use the lock screen for its clock or notifications.
facts: Applies to people who are not required to press Ctrl+Alt+Del to sign in
Enforced by a machine policy, so it applies to every account
Honored on Pro, Enterprise and Education
Revert removes the policy value

name: Show a clear sign-in background
summary: Remove the blur from the sign-in screen background.
what: Sets the policy Show clear logon background, which turns off the acrylic blur behind the sign-in box.
benefit: A sharp sign-in picture instead of a blurred one.
risk: None. Only the look of the sign-in screen changes.
advice: Your choice. It changes how the sign-in screen looks and nothing else.
facts: Enforced by a machine policy, so it applies to every account
Honored on Pro, Enterprise and Education
Needs Windows 10 version 1903 or later
Revert removes the policy value

name: Turn off the Program Compatibility Assistant
summary: No more pop-ups offering compatibility fixes after an older program runs badly.
what: Sets the policy Turn off Program Compatibility Assistant. Windows stops offering solutions to known compatibility problems when programs run.
benefit: No compatibility pop-ups after an older installer or program closes in a way Windows thinks is a problem.
risk: Low. You lose the offered fixes for old programs, and you can still set compatibility options by hand on a program's properties.
advice: Your choice. Useful if the pop-ups only get in your way. Skip it if you run a lot of old software.
facts: No program is changed by this setting
Enforced by a machine policy, so it applies to every account
Honored on Pro, Enterprise and Education
Revert removes the policy value

name: Prefer IPv4 over IPv6
summary: Make Windows try IPv4 first when a site offers both.
what: Sets the IPv6 DisabledComponents value to 0x20, the setting Microsoft documents for preferring IPv4. IPv6 itself stays on.
benefit: Can avoid slow page loads and timeouts on networks where IPv6 is broken or slow, without turning IPv6 off, which Microsoft advises against.
risk: Low. Needs a restart. Sites and services that only offer IPv6 still work, because IPv6 stays on.
advice: Suggested only if connections hang or are slow and IPv6 is the suspect. Most people do not need it.
facts: Microsoft recommends this over disabling IPv6 or unbinding it
Applies to every network adapter on this PC
Only the prefer IPv4 bit (0x20) is changed, so any other IPv6 choice already stored in the value stays as it is
Restart required
Revert puts back the value that was there before

name: Stop Edge suggesting pages for failed addresses
summary: Edge stops sending a mistyped or unreachable address to a web service for suggestions.
what: Applies the Edge policy Suggest similar pages when a webpage can't be found, set to off.
benefit: Addresses that fail to load are not sent to a suggestion service.
risk: None. You just see the plain error page. Edge may show a managed by your organization notice while any policy is set.
advice: Suggested for everyone who would rather not send failed addresses to a web service.
facts: Edge contacts a web service to suggest pages when a connection fails
Also locks the matching switch in Edge settings
Applies to every account
Revert removes the policy value
